title: With hash % N, adding one server sends most keys to a different, empty server
caption: Same key, same hash, new N: k1 now maps to a server that has never cached it, so the read falls through to the database.

messages.label: GET k1 (17 % 3 = 2)
messages.note: 3 servers: hash(k1) = 17, and 17 mod 3 = 2, so k1 lives on S2.

messages.label: scale out: N = 3 → 4
messages.note: Capacity is added. Nothing about k1 changed except N.

messages.label: GET k1 (17 % 4 = 1)
messages.note: 17 mod 4 = 1: the router now asks S1, which has never seen k1.

messages.label: SELECT k1
messages.note: The value is still on S2, but nobody looks there any more. Most keys do this at the same moment, so the database takes nearly the whole read load.

messages.label: GET k6 (25 % 3 = 1 → 25 % 4 = 1)
messages.note: A few keys are lucky: 25 mod 3 and 25 mod 4 are both 1, so k6 stays on S1. Count how many of 8 move in the trace below.
